title: Wren and the Garden
premise: Quentin Eastwick has survived fifteen years in the warded city of Greyhollow by hiding her gift for speaking with beasts, selling harmless charms and keeping her head down. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, she learns her late mother was the last Keeper of a covenant binding the mortal realm to the dragon-fire that fuels all magic—and that Quentin's blood alone can reforge it. Hunted by the Magistrate's wardens and guided by a scarred fox and a dying dragon, she journeys to the ruined Garden where the covenant was first sworn. There she must choose between surrendering her gift forever to seal the pact lawfully, or breaking the old law entirely by swearing a new covenant of shared power—she chooses the latter, reigniting the stars and forcing the realms into an uneasy, just partnership.
about_author: Orsen Fairweather is the pen name of a former botanist who spent a decade cataloguing endangered plants before turning to fantasy. They write stories about stubborn women, talking animals, and gardens that remember more than people do.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. On market day, Quentin sells charms while concealing a conversation with a shop-cat about strange tremors underground. That night the wards shatter and every star vanishes; a wounded fox arrives speaking her mother's name. The beat is dread mixed with reluctant awakening—the life she built on invisibility ends in a single hour.

chapters.title: What the Fox Carried
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, with interludes from Warden Hale tracking her. Fleeing Greyhollow with the fox, Bramble, she learns her mother was the last Keeper and finds a hidden letter naming her heir to the covenant. Hale, who once loved her, hesitates at the kill order. The beat is grief curdling into resolve as inheritance becomes burden.

chapters.title: The Garden Where Fire Sleeps
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the blighted Garden, she meets Emberfall, the last dragon, guttering toward death, and discovers the covenant demands a Keeper's gift be surrendered to renew it. Hale corners her there but, seeing the truth, turns his blade on his own Magistrate instead. The beat is the climax: love against duty made literal, as Quentin refuses both surrender and escape.

chapters.title: A Covenant Rewritten
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She swears a new covenant—not sacrifice but sharing—binding beast-speakers, dragons, and mortals as equals, and the stars relight one by one. Justice comes outside the law: the Magistrate falls to his own wardens' testimony, and magic returns lawful by new terms. The beat is hard-won peace; Quentin plants the Garden anew, no longer hidden.
